::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--description`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Sample description to embed in output files
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `""`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--force_cells`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Define the top N barcodes with the most fragments overlapping peaks as cells and override the cell calling algorithm. N must be a positive integer <= 20,000. Use this option if the number of cells estimated by Cell Ranger ATAC is not consistent with the barcode rank plot
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Max]{.arg-key} `20000`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--peaks`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Override peak caller: specify peaks to use in downstream analyses from supplied 3-column BED file. The supplied peaks file must be sorted by position and not contain overlapping peaks; comment lines beginning with # are allowed
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`file`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"peaks.bed"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--dim_reduce`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Dimensionality reduction mode for clustering
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"lsa"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"lsa"`, `"pca"`, `"plsa"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--subsample_rate`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Downsample to preserve this fraction of reads
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0.1`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--lanes`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
bcl2fastq option. Semicolon-delimited series of lanes to demultiplex. Use this if you have a sample sheet for an entire flow cell but only want to generate a few lanes for further 10x Genomics analysis.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"1,3"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::::

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/mapping/cellranger_atac_count/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline/v4.2.0/components/mapping/cellranger_atac_count);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/mapping/cellranger_atac_count/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
